prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first: do you want a short list of Pleasanton/Bay‑Area lawyers I can pull up for you, or general guidance on how to choose the right injury attorney?

Below is practical, actionable guidance so you can pick the best lawyer for your car‑accident injury case.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get prompt medical treatment and follow doctors’ orders (medical records are key evidence).  
- Take photos of injuries, vehicle damage, scene, skid marks, traffic signs, and clothing.  
- Get police report number and contact info for witnesses.  
- Preserve evidence (your phone, dashcam, damaged clothes).  
- Notify your insurer as required but avoid detailed recorded statements about fault until you talk with a lawyer.  
- Don’t post about the crash or injuries on social media.

Important deadlines
- In California the general personal‑injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the date of injury (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 335.1).  
- If a government vehicle/agency is involved, deadlines can be much shorter (often 6 months to file a claim). Ask a lawyer promptly.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for an attorney who:
- Focuses on car‑accident/personal‑injury work (not a generalist).  
- Has experience handling cases like yours (soft‑tissue vs. catastrophic injury, uninsured motorist, multiple vehicle, DUI, etc.).  
- Has trial experience or a track record of negotiating good settlements — many cases settle, but you want someone willing to go to trial if needed.  
- Is familiar with Alameda County / Tri‑Valley courts and local insurance adjusters.  
- Communicates clearly: who will handle your file day‑to‑day, how often you’ll hear updates, and how to reach them.  
- Has verifiable references, verdicts/settlements, and a clean standing with the California State Bar.

Questions to ask at the initial free consult
- How many car‑accident cases have you handled? How many similar to mine?  
- Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee structure and what costs will be advanced? (Typical contingency fees in CA are roughly 33%–40%, often higher if suit is filed; confirm exact terms.)  
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day? Will junior lawyers/ paralegals be involved?  
- What results have you obtained for similar injuries? Can you provide references?  
- Do you have trial experience? How often do you take cases to trial?  
- How long do you expect this case to take? What is your estimate of value and why?  
- How do you handle medical liens and healthcare provider bills? Who pays upfront costs?  
- Will you provide a written retainer and regular billing for costs?

Documents to bring to the consultation
- Police report (or report number) and collision diagram.  
- Photos or video of the scene, vehicles, and injuries.  
- Medical records, ER notes, imaging (X‑rays, MRIs), and bills.  
- Your insurance policy info (declarations page) and any other drivers’ insurance info.  
- Correspondence from insurers, demand letters, or recorded statement requests.  
- Names and contact info of witnesses.  
- Proof of lost wages (pay stubs) and receipts for expenses related to the crash.

How to verify and compare lawyers
- Check the California State Bar (www.calbar.ca.gov) for license status and discipline history.  
- Read client reviews (Google/Yelp) but weigh them with caution. Look for objective results (verdicts/settlements) and peer recognition.  
- Ask for a written fee agreement and compare net recovery projections after costs and liens.

When to hire quickly
- If the at‑fault party disputes liability, injuries are significant, there are multiple parties, or the claim involves a government entity — hire sooner rather than later to preserve evidence and meet deadlines.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 Pleasanton/Alameda County personal‑injury lawyers with brief notes on experience and contact info.  
- Or, help you draft an email or script for initial consultations.

Tell me which you prefer, and give any details about how serious your injuries were and whether a police report exists.
